back: A copy of data kept separately from the original so it can be restored after loss or damage.
Copies all selected files every time; slowest to make and largest, but quickest to restore.
Copies only files changed since the last backup; quick and small, but restoring needs the last full backup plus every incremental since.
On-site: fast, but lost in the same disaster. Off-site: survives disasters, slow to fetch. Cloud: automatic and off-site, needs internet and a subscription.
Keep three copies of important data, on two types of media, with one copy off-site.
Rebuilds deleted files whose space has not yet been overwritten; stop using the disk until recovery is attempted.
A written, tested plan for protecting data and systems and restoring them after a disaster.

front: Contents of a disaster recovery plan
back: Risk assessment; critical systems; backup policy; recovery procedures; roles and contacts; alternative arrangements; testing and review.
Hardware failure, malware (ransomware), human error, theft, fire, flood, power surges.
